title: Wringer layered requirement evidence
description: `evidence-layers.json` — which gates a requirement needs, when more than one gate speaks to it. A SIBLING of `acceptance.json`, ABSENT when every criterion has at most one binding gate and nothing corroborates, because a single-gate mapping is already fully described there. **Why it exists.** `wringer.acceptance.v3` is frozen and its `gate` and `command` are single values, so it can name one gate per requirement and no more. Until 19 September 2026 the configuration enforced that: `criterion SW-01 is bound more than once` — a refusal with no gates named, no repair printed and no next move. A real requirement can need unit, persistence AND browser evidence; the ZenJev build had exactly that mapping, was refused, and worked around it by nominating one owner gate and documenting the rest in prose that nothing checked. **The relation.** `all-required`: every gate whose `proves:` names the criterion must pass. One that did not run leaves the requirement unproved; one that failed fails it. `corroborates:` is a separate, weaker list: supporting evidence, recorded with its outcome, which **can never override a failure** and never turns an unproved requirement into a proved one. The frozen record still names the first binding gate in declared order as the owner, so an older reader sees a claim that is stricter than or equal to what it would have seen before — never weaker. **What it does not claim.** That the gates together cover the requirement's meaning; that a passing gate is a sufficient test; or that a corroborating gate adds any strength at all, which is why it cannot change a state. Its absence means *no requirement in this run had layered evidence*, never *no requirement needed any*.

relation.description: The one relation this version implements between a criterion's binding gates. Named rather than implied, so a later version that adds alternatives cannot be mistaken for this one.

criteria.description: One row per criterion with layered evidence: more than one binding gate, or at least one corroborating gate. Criteria with a single binding gate and no corroboration are left to acceptance.json.

state.description: The same state acceptance.json recorded for this criterion, repeated so this record can be read alone without inviting a reader to recompute it differently.

owner.description: The first binding gate in declared order — the one acceptance.json's frozen `gate` field names. It has no extra authority: it is the only one that fits in a single-valued field.

proved_by.description: Every gate whose `proves:` names this criterion, in declared order. All of them must pass.

status.description: `did-not-run` is its own outcome: a gate that was not selected, or was skipped after an earlier failure, has not failed and has not passed.

receipt.description: The sealed earlier record showing this same gate genuinely failing, or null when none was found. Every binding gate needs one before the criterion is evidenced; the frozen record carries the owner's.

corroborated_by.description: Gates whose `corroborates:` names this criterion, with their outcomes. Recorded and never decisive: a failure here does not fail the requirement, and a pass here cannot rescue one.

reason.description: The sentence a person reads, naming the gate that decided this row.

limits.description: What this record does NOT claim, travelling with it. Pinned by CONTENT in the tests.
